the presence of aggressive ER-negative breast cancer cells can increase the metastatic potential for ER-positive breast cancer cells, and that cell fusion in a metastatic niche can result in the generation of hybrid cells with metastatic properties.

the presence of aggressive ER negative orthotopically growing breast cancer tumors in mouse resulted in the generation of a novel metastatic hybrid cell line, which has stem-like properties and metastatic to the brain.
cell-cell fusion between breast cancer cells in the bone can result in the emergence of a new cell line with stem-like properties and metastatic potential.

the origin and contribution of tumor heterogeneity in breast cancer progression.
the effect of the presence of heterogeneous cells on each other's metastasis.
the generation and characterization of a novel metastatic hybrid cell line B 6TC generated by the fusion of ER negative and ER positive breast cancer cells in mouse bone marrow.

cell fusion can be an important mechanism for tumor heterogeneity and metastatic progression of cancer cells.
